t:
Part A of title II of the Act is amended by inserting at the end thereof a new section as follows:


“assistance for planning and other preliminary expenses of proposed housing projects under section 221 of the national housing act
“Sec. 207. 

(a) 
In order to encourage and facilitate the construction or rehabilitation of housing to meet the needs of low- and moderate income families and individuals, the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (hereafter in this section referred to as the ‘Secretary’) is authorized to make grants and loans from the Appalachian Housing Fund established by this section, under such terms and conditions as he may prescribe, to nonprofit, limited dividend, or cooperative organizations, or to public bodies, for expenses of planning and of obtaining an insured mortgage for a housing construction or rehabilitation project, under section 221 of the National Housing Act (hereafter in this section referred to as ‘section 221’), in any area of the Appalachian 
region determined by the Commission to have significant potential for future growth.


“(b) 
No grant under this section shall exceed 80 per centum of those administrative expenses, incident to planning a project and obtaining an insured mortgage under section 221, which the Secretary considers not to be recoverable from the proceeds of a mortgage insured under such section: Provided, That no grant shall be made to an organization established for profit.


“(c) 
No loan under this section shall exceed 80 per centum of the cost of planning a project and obtaining an insured mortgage under section 221, including, but not limited to, preliminary surveys and analyses of market needs, preliminary site engineering and architectural fees, site options, Federal Housing Administration and Federal National Mortgage Association fees, and construction loan fees and discounts. Loans may be made without interest, or at any market or below market interest rate authorized for a mortgage insured under section 221: Provided, That any loan made to an organization established for profit shall bear interest at the prevailing market rate authorized for a mortgage insured under such section. The Secretary may, except in the case of a loan to an organization established for profit, waive the repayment of all or any part of a loan made under this section, including interest, which he finds the borrower is unable to recover from the proceeds of a mortgage insured under section 221.


“(d) 
All funds allocated to the Secretary for the purposes of this section shall be deposited in a fund which shall be known as the Appalachian Housing Fund and shall be used as a revolving fund by the Secretary for carrying out such purposes. General expenses of administration of this section may be charged to the fund. Moneys in the fund not needed for current operation may be invested in bonds or other obligations guaranteed as to principal and interest by the United States.


“(e) 
Not to exceed $5,000,000 of the funds authorized in section 401 of this Act for the two-fiscal-year period ending June 30, 1969, shall be available to carry out this section.”

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this is only a grant and loan program, and applications for grants or loans are not participation. However, the Secretary may fund projects only in areas that the Commission determines have significant growth potential. In the Appalachian Regional Development Act, the Commission is the Appalachian Regional Commission, a federal-state body whose members include representatives of the Appalachian states, so non-federal actors help shape where federal money goes. The section does not itself describe the Commission's membership, so this rests on background knowledge and is a close call.
fable.s: determined by the Commission to have significant potential for future growth

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes the Secretary to provide grants and loans to outside entities for planning and preliminary expenses. According to the definition, applications for benefits or grants are explicitly excluded from participation. The text describes a funding mechanism where outside parties apply for or receive funds, rather than a process where they consult with or advise the government on a decision.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development ... is authorized to make grants and loans ... to nonprofit, limited dividend, or cooperative organizations, or to public bodies, for expenses of planning and of obtaining an insured mortgage

opus.w: This section sets up a grant and loan fund for planning expenses, and the definition excludes applications for benefits, grants and loans from participation. The tempting 'Yes' reading relies on the Appalachian Regional Commission's determination of growth areas, since that body includes state members. However, that determination comes from a separate, existing function, and this section creates no new consultation, hearing, comment period or rulemaking requirement. 'Terms and conditions as he may prescribe' does not expressly call for regulations either.
opus.s: is authorized to make grants and loans from the Appalachian Housing Fund established by this section, under such terms and conditions as he may prescribe, to nonprofit, limited dividend, or cooperative organizations, or to public bodies
opus.b: **Tempting reading:** the grants and loans to nonprofits and public bodies look like outside parties taking part. They don't count, because applying for grants or loans is not participation. A closer question is the reference to "the Commission." This is presumably the Appalachian Regional Commission, a federal-state body that includes state governors. Grants are limited to areas "determined by the Commission," so the section could be read as giving outsiders a role in gating a federal decision. But the section creates no consultation, hearing, comment period or rulemaking step of its own. It only points to a determination the Commission already makes under a separate part of the Act. I lean "No," but not strongly.

qwen_chat.w: The definition explicitly states that applications for benefits or grants are not participation. This section authorizes the Secretary to make grants to outside entities, which falls under this exclusion. It looks like participation because it involves grants to outside organizations.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (hereafter in this section referred to as the ‘Secretary’) is authorized to make grants and loans from the Appalachian Housing Fund established by this section, under such terms and conditions as he may prescribe, to nonprofit, limited dividend, or cooperative organizations, or to public bodies, for expenses of planning and of obtaining an insured mortgage for a housing construction or rehabilitation project
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it involves grants to outside organizations.
Resolution: The definition explicitly states that applications for benefits or grants are not participation. This section authorizes the Secretary to make grants to outside entities, which falls under this exclusion.
